target_customer: Millennial consumers wanting a free mobile-first checking account and debit card
problem: Big banks charge fees and penalties and are disliked by younger customers; Cheddar pitched a free, powerful mobile checking account as the fix.
business_model: Consumer neobank on a partner bank, revenue model not stated in sources (YC page mentions a new business model, interchange likely but unconfirmed)
product_category: Mobile checking account and debit card (neobank)

founders.name: Brian Brunner
prior_employers: Stripe (engineering manager who led the team that built Sigma and Data Pipeline, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Education not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Moven
competitors.what: Mobile-first bank account and app built on a partner bank, focused on spending insight
competitors.traction_then: Left beta in March 2014 and opened sign-ups to everyone

competitors.name: Simple
competitors.what: Mobile banking service on partner banks with a debit card and check deposit
competitors.traction_then: Public launch in July 2012; reportedly about 80,000 customers by late 2013

competitors.name: Bluebird (American Express)
competitors.what: Prepaid checking-style account with check requests, named alongside Moven and Simple

technical_complexity.rationale: A two person team had to integrate with a partner bank (Metropolitan Commercial Bank per a 2014 Bank Innovation article), card issuing and links to Ally, Wealthfront, Lending Club and Coinbase, which is standard fintech engineering with regulatory plumbing.

defensibility.rationale: Simple and Moven already offered similar partner-bank accounts, the product was an interface on someone else's bank charter, and no network effect or proprietary data is described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established banks and Bluebird already offered competing accounts; the sources do not say whether any copied Cheddar specifically.

market_need_then: The YC page cites a claim that nearly 3 of 4 millennials would rather go to the dentist than listen to their bank and complains of fee-heavy checking accounts; 2014 coverage shows a wave of mobile banks (Simple, Moven, Bluebird, GoBank).

branding.domain_note: Used cheddar.io (not a .com); as of 2026 the domain redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful anti-bank copy on the YC page (dentist joke, evil banks).

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; the name is a money slang pun that was shared by many later companies (UK rewards app Cheddar, Cheddar Up), so it was confusable; the playful voice on the YC page is the only identity evidence.

outcome_analysis: Cheddar was a two founder YC S14 neobank that raised a seed round syndicated by S2 Capital and used a partner bank, but the shutdown date and cause are not public; the YC directory marks it Inactive and cheddar.io is now parked for sale. Direct competitors Simple and Moven were ahead, and the cause of failure is left empty because no source states it.
notes: Shutdown cause and date not public; searches (outcome, funding, cross-check) found only the YC Inactive status. The seed round rests on one outlet (Bank Innovation, read only through search summaries because bankinnovation.net could not be fetched) and gives no amount. Reports of a 1.25M seed led by M25 Group concern a different company named Cheddar (software monetization) and were excluded. Competitor sources were seen as search results, not opened in full.
